A measure of clustering among aromatic residues
Long Description of Computation: First, counts the number of closely clustered aromatic residues (CCAR; defined as a F/Y/W residue which is followed by another F/Y/W residue within the next 5 amino acids). Then computes an expectation and variance of the number of CCARs based on the percentage of F/Y/W, based on a binomial null sequence model. Finally, uses the expectation and variance of CCARs to turn the raw CCAR count into a z-score, which is the reported number. Higher means more aromatic clusters than expected by chance, lower means more disperse/uniform aromatics.
Additional Info: This measure was developed in house, but meant to be interpreted the same as aromatic omega (Ω_π) in this paper: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/34863777/

Short Description of Computation: A measure of sequence complexity (see citation)
Long Description of Computation: The log (natural) of the number of distinct permutations of the sequence, divided by sequence length. Sequences with a composition profile dominated by a few residue kinds will have less distinct permutations (lower complexity), while sequences with a balanced composition profile with many kinds of residues will have more distinct permutations (higher complexity).
Additional Info: Paper in which this measure was introduced: https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/009784859385006X

Short Description of Computation: A measure of charge clustering
Long Description of Computation: First, counts the number of closely clustered same-charge residues (CCSCR; defined as a D/E/K/R residue which is followed by another D/E/K/R residue of the same charge within the next 5 amino acids). Then computes an expectation and variance of the number of CCSCRs based on the composition of D/E and K/R, based on a binomial null sequence model. Finally, uses the expectation and variance of CCSCRs to turn the raw CCSCR count into a z-score, which is the reported number. Higher means more same charge clusters than expected by chance, lower means more disperse/uniform charge distribution.
Additional Info: This measure was developed in house, but meant to be interpreted the same as kappa (κ) in this paper: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5232785/

Short Description of Computation: A measure of clustering among disorder-promoting residues
Long Description of Computation: First, counts the number of closely clustered disorder-promoting residues (CCDPR; defined as a D/E/K/R/P residue which is followed by another D/E/K/R/P residue within the next 5 amino acids). Then computes an expectation and variance of the number of CCDPRs based on the percentage of D/E/K/R/P, based on a binomial null sequence model. Finally, uses the expectation and variance of CCDPRs to turn the raw CCDPR count into a z-score, which is the reported number. Higher means more disorder-promoting clusters than expected by chance, lower means more disperse/uniform disorder-promoting residue distribution.
Additional Info: This measure was developed in house, but meant to be interpreted the same as omega (Ω_{D,E,K,R,P}) in this paper: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10178624/
